versions.author: c_grant
versions.content:
# The State of AP 2026: what 400 finance leaders told us

1. 64% of finance leaders say their AP team spends too much time on manual invoice entry (73% at companies
   without AP automation).
2. Teams that use AP automation close their books 2.3 days faster on average (6.3 vs 8.6 days).
3. ERP change is a trigger: 45% plan an ERP change in 2027.
4. The pain isn't about size: it's about automation.

Methodology: online survey of 400 US finance decision-makers at companies with $50M-$1B revenue, recruited from
opt-in B2B panels, October 19-30, 2026; results are not weighted.

documents.title: Press release final: State of AP 2026

versions.author: c_monica
versions.content:
# Arbeline research: nearly two-thirds of mid-market finance teams are still buried in manual invoice entry

DENVER, Nov. 6, 2026 -- A new survey of 400 U.S. finance decision-makers from Arbeline, the AP automation
company, finds that 64% say their AP team spends too much time on manual invoice entry, rising to 73% at
companies without AP automation, and that teams using AP automation close their books 2.3 days faster on
average. 45% plan an ERP change in 2027.

Methodology: online survey of 400 U.S. finance decision-makers at companies with $50 million to $1 billion in
revenue, recruited from opt-in B2B panels, October 19-30, 2026, fielded by Penmore Research; results are not
weighted.

versions.author: c_ben
versions.content:
# Q32 "What is the hardest part of AP at your company today?": coding summary (draft)

Base: 312 valid respondents who answered Q32 (of 400 valid). 418 codes assigned (multi-coded, up to 3).

| Code | Mentions | % of respondents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approvals stuck in email or with one approver | 104 | 24.9% |
| Manual keying and re-keying | 92 | 22.0% |
| ERP sync and coding errors | 71 | 17.0% |

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Readout Q&A prep (for the 11:15 dry run)

1. Why no margin of error? Opt-in panel, not a probability sample; we describe the sample instead (400 valid, $50M-$1B, Oct 19-30, unweighted).
2. Why 400 and not 438? 38 removed under the SOW's four quality rules; the WTP tables were rerun on the 400.
3. Does automation make teams close 2.3 days faster? We can say automation users close faster on average (6.3 vs 8.6 days), not that automation causes it: bigger or better-run teams may adopt it first. Correlation, not causation.
4. Is $599 supported? It's above the indifference point ($590), inside the acceptable range ($405-$700); the research supports $515-$590, the price is the committee's call.
5. Is the band difference in pain real? No: 60 / 65 / 69% is not significant; the automation difference is.
6. Are the awareness gaps significant? Directional: same respondents rate every vendor; Penmore can run paired tests.
7. What share call $575 too expensive? Not in the intersection table; we'd need Penmore's cumulative curves.
